situation:
You are the financial analyst at ARDEN AEROSTRUCTURES, a supplier of machined structural parts for commercial aircraft. The vice president of finance (judge) has asked you to review this year's capital requests and bring a recommendation, because the requests add up to more than the company has to spend.

Eight months ago the company merged with KESTREL MACHINE WORKS, and the two plants still run separate schedules, separate part numbers, and separate maintenance records. The finance group is adding two analyst positions to carry the combined reporting. A new spend-analysis system pulls both plants into one set of figures for the first time, and the board approved a single capital budget for the year.

The figures rank an automated inspection cell at the KESTREL MACHINE WORKS plant first by a wide margin, and the figures behind that request were prepared by the plant that submitted it. The second request is a replacement heat-treat furnace at the legacy plant. The furnace passes inspection and its measured downtime is low, but the supervisors who have run it for two decades say it is failing in ways the maintenance log does not capture.

Funding the inspection cell follows the numbers and speeds the plant the merger was meant to bring on, but leaves the furnace in place, and a furnace failure would halt certified production for months while the customer requalifies another source. Funding the furnace answers people who know the equipment, but spends the year on a project whose payback the figures cannot show, and the acquired plant will read it as the merger favoring the old company.

Splitting the budget between the two would start both and finish neither this year. The vice president of finance (judge) wants your assessment of the risk carried by each request and a recommendation on where the year's capital goes. The vice president of finance (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the vice president of finance (judge) at ARDEN AEROSTRUCTURES. Business background is the same as the situation above. You approved the spend-analysis system, you inherited two plants that have not yet been brought together, and you have one capital budget for the year. You want the financial analyst to assess the risk carried by each request and to recommend where the year's capital goes.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and listen to the presentation without steering it. After the presentation, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how would we know this was the right call?
What would tell us we chose wrong?
